newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Great Eastern Shipping sets FRN.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Great Eastern Shipping sets FRN.

text.p: Asian debt markets were slow on Wednesday following a hectic session the previous day.

India's Great Eastern Shipping set a US$50 million seven-year floating rate note issue. The notes pay a margin of 135 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate. Fees are 62.5 basis points.
ANZ Banking Group, which is active in arranging financing for Indian names, lead managed the issue.
Indian capital markets issues have been rare recently, with most borrowers opting for syndicated loans.

Investors have been wary of taking on Indian names for seven years, which is the minimum tenor permitted under Indian law for most issuers. Only a few institutions, notably the policy banks such as ICICI and IDBI, can borrow for a shorter period.
Another Indian corporate also is in the market at this time. Videocon is seeking US$70 million via a seven-year FRN issue arranged by Peregrine Fixed Income.
In the loan market, the facility for Hong Kong's CITIC Pacific has been increased to HK$3.8 billion from HK$3.5 billion following an enthusiastic response in the underwriting phase.
Including coordinating arrangers Chase Manhattan Asia, HSBC Investment Bank and J.P. Morgan Securities, 26 banks joined as arrangers and lead managers.
And Shun Tak Holdings today confirmed a Shun Tak-led consortium is seeking a loan of about HK$6.4 billion to fund its Belcher Gardens project in Hong Kong.
Looking ahead, the US$1 billion global bond for Malaysia's Petronas may launch later today.
